title: Linear Equations
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Linear Equations. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
One-variable equations

An equation states that two expressions have equal values. Preserve equality by applying the same operation to both sides. For (\(ax+b=c\)), isolate (\(x\)) using inverse operations. If (\(a=0\)), the equation is either impossible or true for every value, depending on the remaining constants.

Brackets and fractions

Expand or clear denominators carefully. Multiplying every term of an equation by a common nonzero denominator removes fractions without changing its solution.

Simultaneous equations

A pair of linear equations represents two lines. Their intersection is the solution. Substitution replaces one variable using an equation; elimination adds or subtracts equations to cancel a variable. Parallel distinct lines give no solution; coincident lines give infinitely many.

Worked example: Solve (\(3(2x-1)=2x+13\)). Expanding gives (\(6x-3=2x+13\)), so (\(4x=16\)) and (\(x=4\)). Substitution into the original gives (\(3(8-1)=21\)) and (\(8+13=21\)).

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Keep a clear line for each equality-preserving operation.
  • When clearing fractions, multiply every term on both sides.
  • In a word problem, define the unknown and its unit before forming an equation.
  • Check in the original equation, especially after clearing denominators.
  • For two equations, choose elimination when coefficients can be matched quickly.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• Adding or subtracting the same expression on both sides preserves equality.
  • Division by a coefficient is allowed only if it is nonzero.
  • For (\(ax+b=cx+d\)), if (a neq c), then (\(x=(d-b)/(a-c)\)).
  • Two linear equations can have one, none or infinitely many solutions.

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    Solve (\(5x-7=28\)).

    1. (\(5\))
    2. (\(6\))
    3. (\(7\))
    4. (\(8\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(7\))

    Add 7: (\(5x=35\)); divide by 5 to get (\(x=7\)).

  2. Core:

    If (\(2x+y=11\)) and (\(x=4\)), what is (\(y\))?

    1. (\(1\))
    2. (\(2\))
    3. (\(3\))
    4. (\(4\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(3\))

    Substitute (\(x=4\)): (\(8+y=11\)), so (\(y=3\)).

  3. Foundation:

    Solve (\(4x+7=31\)).

    1. (\(4\))
    2. (\(5\))
    3. (\(6\))
    4. (\(7\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(6\))

    Subtract 7 to get (\(4x=24\)); divide by 4, so (\(x=6\)).

  4. Standard:

    Solve (\(2(x-3)=x+5\)).

    1. (\(7\))
    2. (\(9\))
    3. (\(11\))
    4. (\(13\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(11\))

    Expand to get (\(2x-6=x+5\)). Subtract (\(x\)) and add 6: (\(x=11\)).

  5. Challenge:

    Solve the system (\(2x+y=11\)) and (\(x-y=1\)).

    1. (\((3,5)\))
    2. (\((4,3)\))
    3. (\((5,1)\))
    4. (\((6,-1)\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\((4,3)\))

    Add the equations: (\(3x=12\)), so (\(x=4\)). Then (\(4-y=1\)), giving (\(y=3\)). The solution is (\((4,3)\)).
